beats.narration: You're left holding the heavy bag of your own empathy. You invest deeply in a human life and the narrative just buries them in the dirt and coldly moves on to the next century.
I hear that frustration, but I argue that that specific discomfort is exactly the profound point of the entire experience.
As humans, we are deeply narcissistically conditioned to think we are the main characters of the universe.
We think our loves and our wars are the center of reality. This narrative brutally forces us to look in the mirror and realize the humbling truth.
Humans aren't the grand tragic heroes of the earth. And we aren't even the grand apocalyptic villains. To the deep time with the forest, we are
just seasonal crops. We sprout up. We make a tremendous amount of noise and mess. And then we are inevitably harvested by time,
rotting down to feed the soil for whatever beautiful wild thing needs to grow next. So the next time you are walking through a quiet, peaceful
patch of woods, I want you to look down at the slight unnatural bumps in the earth.
Look at the weird sharp angle of a massive
pine branch. Ask yourself what incredibly violent, profoundly
